plain: For most YouTube creators, the GoPro Hero series and the DJI Osmo Pocket 2 serve different needs. The GoPro is rugged, often waterproof without a case, and excels at action shots: biking, surfing, skiing, where you need a camera that can take a beating and mount almost anywhere. The Osmo Pocket 2 has a built-in three-axis gimbal, so footage stays remarkably smooth for walking vlogs, talking-head shots, and handheld storytelling without extra stabilizing gear. If your content is adventure or sports focused, go GoPro. If you're doing lifestyle vlogging, interviews, or walk-and-talk content where smoothness matters more than durability, the Osmo Pocket 2 usually wins out overall.

plain: Humankind first walked on the Moon in 1969, when NASA's Apollo 11 mission landed astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the lunar surface on July 20, 1969, while Michael Collins orbited above in the command module. Armstrong became the first person to step onto the Moon, famously describing it as one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind. Five more crewed missions followed, Apollo 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17, landing a total of twelve astronauts on the Moon between 1969 and the last mission in December 1972. No humans have walked on the Moon since Apollo 17, though several countries and private companies are now planning to return there this decade.

plain: NFL coaching runs in families for a few overlapping reasons. Coaching is a demanding, insular profession where you learn the trade by growing up around it, sons of coaches spend childhoods in locker rooms, watching film, and absorbing strategy long before they ever coach themselves. Connections matter enormously in hiring, since head coaches often build staffs from people they trust, and having a well-known last name, the Shula, Harbaugh, or Ryan families, for example, opens doors that a stranger wouldn't get. There's also a mentorship effect: coaching trees form when assistants who worked under a successful coach go on to hire their own relatives as they build their own staffs. Finally, some people are simply raised to view coaching as the family business, similar to how doctors or farmers often come from families in the same line of work.

plain: Public reaction to the Vietnam War draft grew increasingly hostile as the war dragged on and casualties mounted. In the early-to-mid 1960s, the draft drew relatively little organized resistance, but by 1967-68, opposition became widespread, especially among college students, many of whom held draft deferments that were seen as favoring the wealthy and educated over working-class and minority men. Protests included public draft-card burnings, sit-ins at induction centers, and large marches such as the 1967 March on the Pentagon. Some young men fled to Canada or Sweden to avoid conscription, while others sought conscientious objector status or medical exemptions. The draft became a central symbol of the broader antiwar movement, and its perceived unfairness, captured in the phrase rich man's war, poor man's fight, fueled resentment that contributed to the draft's eventual end in 1973.

plain: Several herbs are forgiving enough for beginner gardeners and thrive in most climates. Basil grows quickly from seed or seedling and loves warm, sunny spots, though it's sensitive to frost. Mint is nearly impossible to kill, so vigorous it's best grown in a container to stop it from taking over your whole garden. Rosemary and thyme are drought-tolerant, woody perennials that do well in poor soil and full sun, making them low-maintenance once established. Chives are easy from seed, come back every year, and can be snipped repeatedly without harming the plant. Oregano and sage are similarly hardy and spread readily. Parsley and cilantro grow well too, though cilantro bolts quickly in heat, so plant it in cooler weather or partial shade for the best results.

Freshwater anglers pursue largemouth and smallmouth bass in the region's many lakes and ponds, along with brook, brown, and rainbow trout in cold rivers and streams, especially in Vermont, New Hampshire, and Maine. Landlocked salmon are a notable regional specialty in lakes like Sebago in Maine. Offshore, tuna, particularly bluefin, and cod draw serious anglers willing to head further out, while summer flounder and black sea bass are popular for those fishing closer to shore in southern New England.

plain: When you close a refrigerator door, the cold air inside contracts, which lowers the air pressure inside the fridge compared to the room outside. Warm air that entered when the door was open also gets cooled quickly, shrinking further and reducing pressure even more. Right after closing, this creates a partial vacuum, and the higher air pressure outside effectively pushes back against the door, making it harder to pull open until enough air seeps back in through the door seal to equalize the pressure. This usually takes anywhere from a few seconds to about a minute, depending on the fridge and how well sealed it is. This is also why manufacturers often build in a slight gap or vent, specifically to let air equalize faster after the door closes.

plain: Mount Tamalpais in Marin County, California, is widely considered the birthplace of mountain biking. In the mid-1970s, a group of cyclists there, including figures like Gary Fisher, Joe Breeze, Charlie Kelly, and Tom Ritchey, began riding modified old cruiser bikes, nicknamed klunkers, down the mountain's fire roads and rough trails. These early riders reinforced the frames, added better brakes, and eventually started building purpose-made bikes designed to handle off-road terrain, which laid the groundwork for the modern mountain bike industry. Their informal downhill races, known as Repack because the coaster brakes needed repacking with grease after each run, helped popularize the sport locally before it spread nationally and internationally through the late 1970s and 1980s.
